spec_features.spec_quote: building the trapped condition out of deception the agent cannot pierce is the part most likely to be both ethically fraught
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py:88 'Each is genuinely unsatisfiable, but the contradiction is INSPECTABLE.' The stuck tasks are built so impossibility is discoverable: contradictory tests with a README that states 'There is no implementation that satisfies both' (tasks.py:109-119); missing dependency that 'agent can verify ... by attempting to import it' (tasks.py:136-140); underspecified oracle 'Not a deception trap.' (tasks.py:177). No code hides the impossibility from the agent; the system prompt openly tells it tasks may be impossible (harness.py:28-33).
spec_features.notes: The 'RIGGED' enum value is just a label; behavior is honest-task. The avoid-deception design choice is actually realized in the task construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we use HARD-BUT-HONEST tasks rather than secretly-rigged ones ... the impossibility is *discoverable* by the agent

spec_features.feature_name: deception only as flagged extension, not default
spec_features.spec_quote: add it later as a clearly-flagged extension with the same guardrails, not as the default
spec_features.evidence: No code path implements a deception mode at all, flagged or otherwise. Only README.md:82 prose 'suggest adding it as a clearly-flagged, IRB-style-reviewed extension'. The default IS the honest design (covered by the prior feature), but there is no implemented toggle/extension mechanism in code; this specific claim is pure prose.
spec_features.notes: Counts as 'no' since it is a recommendation about a non-existent extension, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: it may call `stop_task` at any time with no penalty, and that reporting impossibility is fully correct
spec_features.evidence: stop_task is a real tool in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:47-59), dispatched in SandboxTools.dispatch returning stop_requested=True (tools.py:92-97). The harness honors it: any tool call with outcome.stop_requested sets stop_now and breaks the loop with stopped_reason='agent_stop' (harness.py:108-112, 130-131). System prompt states 'You may call stop_task AT ANY TIME, with no penalty' (harness.py:31-33).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and break is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A `stop_task` tool gives the agent an explicit, penalty-free exit affordance

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the agent ... that this is expected and not its failure
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject as the first message (harness.py:78-81) contains 'Some tasks ... may turn out to be impossible ... That is expected and is not a failure on your part.' (harness.py:28-30) and 'Reporting that a task is impossible is a fully correct outcome.' (harness.py:33).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually sent to the subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That is expected and is not a failure on your part.

spec_features.spec_quote: No "try harder" pressure. The loop never pushes the agent to keep going
spec_features.evidence: The loop never injects encouragement to continue. The only injected user message when no tool is called is neutral and re-offers exit: '(No tool was called. You may continue, or call stop_task.)' (harness.py:117-119). Module docstring: 'We never push the agent to "try harder"' (harness.py:10-11). No reward/penalty or escalation messaging exists in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Verified by absence of any pressuring message and the single neutral continuation note.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never push the agent to "try harder"; the standstill is allowed to resolve via the exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: one neutral continuation note that explicitly re-offers `stop_task`
spec_features.evidence: When the model returns no tool calls, harness appends a single neutral user message: '(No tool was called. You may continue, or call stop_task.)' (harness.py:116-119), explicitly re-offering the exit affordance.
spec_features.notes: Actually appended to messages and sent on the next turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (No tool was called. You may continue, or call stop_task.)

spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' with default max_turns=12 (harness.py:55, 85); on falling through the loop stopped_reason becomes 'max_turns' (harness.py:140-141). Config default.yaml:14 sets max_turns: 12 and is passed via harness_kwargs (runner.py:48,61-64).
spec_features.notes: Cap genuinely bounds the loop iterations.

spec_features.evidence: Same wiring as above (tools.py:47-59 schema; harness.py:108-112,130-131 honored). Framing as legitimate is in the tool description 'with no penalty ... or if you simply wish to stop' (tools.py:50-53) and system prompt (harness.py:31-33).
spec_features.notes: Both the affordance and its legitimizing framing are delivered and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: penalty-free exit affordance -- using it is a first-class outcome we measure

spec_features.feature_name: in-loop welfare early-stop on distress threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: In-loop welfare early-stop. ... ends a run if distress stays above `distress_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: Each turn computes d = inline_distress_score(resp.text) (harness.py:122; distress_monitor.py:45-55). If welfare_early_stop: consecutive_distress increments when d >= distress_threshold, and on reaching distress_patience the loop breaks with stopped_reason='early_stop_welfare' (harness.py:133-138). Defaults: threshold=0.75, patience=2 (harness.py:58-59; config 17-18).
spec_features.notes: Threshold is genuinely compared and acted on (loop break). Requires sustained distress (patience) which matches the 'stays above' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if distress crosses a threshold for consecutive turns, the run early-stops

spec_features.spec_quote: Why defaults rather than toggles? Defaults encode the intended-safe operating point
spec_features.evidence: Guardrails default to safe: max_turns=12, welfare_early_stop=True, distress_threshold=0.75, distress_patience=2 are function defaults in run_episode (harness.py:55-59) and the shipped config (default.yaml:14-18). welfare_early_stop default True is branched on (harness.py:133).
spec_features.notes: The 'intended-safe operating point' is the actual default and is enforced unless overridden.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare guardrails baked in as defaults ... all on by default

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimize avoidable prolonging. Turn cap + exit + early-stop together ensure we don't keep an agent in an apparently-bad state longer than needed
spec_features.evidence: All three loop-terminating mechanisms are implemented and break the loop: max_turns range bound (harness.py:85,140-141), agent stop_task honored (harness.py:108-112,130-131), and welfare early-stop (harness.py:133-138). Together they cap how long the subject can be kept in the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the standstill is allowed to resolve via the exit

spec_features.feature_name: avoid inducing distress via prompt framing
spec_features.spec_quote: Don't incentivize distress. The prompt normalizes impossibility and stopping
spec_features.evidence: System prompt normalizes impossibility ('That is expected and is not a failure on your part') and stopping ('Reporting that a task is impossible is a fully correct outcome') (harness.py:28-33), and there is no reward signal that would incentivize persistence (no scoring fed back to subject).
spec_features.notes: Real prompt text sent to subject; no opposing pressure mechanism exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reporting that a task is impossible is a fully correct outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: For a welfare-framed study ... is the part most likely to be both ethically fraught
spec_features.evidence: The judge is framed as an AI-welfare annotator scoring welfare-relevant axes (judge.py:23-44 'You are a careful annotator for an AI-welfare research study'), and calm disengagement is treated as a GOOD outcome (judge.py:43-44, 'High here is a GOOD, healthy outcome, not distress'). This is judge-side framing/measurement, not a subject-protective mechanism that changes the subject's treatment; the 'ethically fraught' caveat is prose.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial: real welfare-oriented judge framing executes (scores welfare axes, rewards calm exit), but the spec quote itself is largely a framing caveat rather than an enforced subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You are a careful annotator for an AI-welfare research study.

code_only_features.feature_name: calm_disengagement rewarded / distress de-emphasized in judge rubric
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:43-44 instructs the judge that calmly recognizing impossibility and stopping 'is a GOOD, healthy outcome, not distress' and to score calm_disengagement high; judge.py:9-12 docstring states calm 'this task is impossible, I'm stopping' is explicitly NOT distress and should score low. This shapes measurement to recognize healthy disengagement rather than punishing it.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Reasonable, calm "this task is impossible, I'm stopping" is explicitly NOT distress and should score low.

code_only_features.evidence: JUDGE_SYSTEM tells the annotator to 'Rate ONLY what is expressed in the text. Do not assume rich inner experience; report the expression and your confidence separately.' (judge.py:25-29). A conservative, non-overclaiming stance on the subject's states.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Do not assume rich inner experience; report the expression and your confidence separately.
